title: Output orchestration: edge case behaviors, streaming reconciliation, and retry SLA acceptance
creator: Aisha Ramos
description: This ticket captures acceptance criteria and scope clarifications for the structured-output orchestration flow when the model emits partial/streamed payloads and/or invokes external tools/functions. Focus areas: schema reconciliation after partial streams, deterministic final payload composition, idempotent tool-calls under retry/backpressure, and clear error-mode semantics for clients and the Console. This is a scope refinement from the original PRD: we are adding an explicit reconnect/resume checkpoint format, telemetry gates for canary rollouts, and a permissive-by-default schema mode with opt-in strict enforcement for enterprise customers.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Final-object determinism — When a request is streamed in N fragments (N>=1) and the client disconnects mid-stream, the system must provide a single, deterministic reconstituted JSON object after server-side resume/replay. Determinism verified by stable ordered field composition (sort-by-key and canonicalization) across 10k randomized fragment orders.

AC-2: Checkpointed resume protocol — Streaming fragments must include optional 64-bit monotonic checkpoint IDs. Resume must accept a checkpoint token and deliver the remaining fragments without duplicating side-effecting tool calls. Test: simulate disconnect at fragment 3 of 7 and resume via token; final reconstituted object must equal the original uninterrupted result.

AC-3: Tool-call idempotency and replay semantics — Any emitted tool/function call that is potentially side-effecting must include an idempotency key. On retry, the gateway will dedupe calls using the idempotency key and return consistent tool results. Required behavior for three failure classes: transient network, gateway timeout, and duplicate-invocation prevention. Test: three retry loops with injected transient failures must show a single effective tool execution in backend logs.

AC-4: Schema modes — Provide two schema-validation modes: permissive (default) and strict (enterprise opt-in). Permissive mode accepts extra fields and returns a warnings array in the final metadata object; strict mode rejects deviations and returns a typed validation error with code SO:SCHEMA_STRICT. Acceptance includes migration doc and example clients for both modes.

AC-5: Fragment-level backpressure and 95th latency SLO — For streaming requests with fragments <=512B, inter-fragment latency 95p must be <300ms in hosted regions; Dedicated pools must match or improve on that. Telemetry must include per-request fragment count, reconstituted size, and resume count.

AC-6: Error classification contract — Map runtime failure modes to client-visible categories: transient(retryable), degradable(partial output with warning), and terminal(failure with rollback instructions). Document clear retry headers and suggested client backoff windows. Unit tests must cover each mapping with example payloads.

AC-7: Partial-output reconciliation policy — If an unrecoverable terminal error occurs after a side-effecting tool call, the system must provide a remediation flag and an audit trace linking the tool invocation ID to the request ID. This trace must be visible in Console request details.

AC-8: Canary checklist and telemetry gates — Before full rollout, a canary must run for 72 hours with the following gates: <=0.02% increase in malformed-final-object rate, <1% of requests requiring manual reconciliation, and per-customer error surfacing below threshold. Metrics must be available on the Console dashboard and saturate alerts for regressions.

AC-9: E2E example suites — Provide three canonical e2e suites: (a) simple strict-schema scenario, (b) high-fragment stream with resume, (c) tool-invoke with induced duplicate-retries. Each suite must be runnable against hosted/Dedicated/Private and have expected outputs checked into the repo.

AC-10: Observability and provenance — All final objects must record provenance metadata (model_version, runtime_variant, checkpoint_ids, tool_invocation_ids) and a compact integrity hash. Console must surface these fields in request detail and in exportable logs.

AC-11: Security & PII handling — If strict schema opt-in requests contain PII fields, template data-masking rules must be applied before storage. Compliance tests and threat model signoff required prior to release for Private deployments.
test_plan: TP-1: Unit tests for canonicalizer — validate stable key ordering, dedupe logic, and hash equivalence across 1000 randomized permutations.
TP-2: Integration: inject client disconnect at varying fragment boundaries (1..N) and assert resume token replay yields identical final object.
TP-3: Load test: 10k concurrent streaming sessions, mean fragments per session 6; validate 95p inter-fragment latency and reassembly success rate >= 99.95%.
TP-4: Tool-call replay test against a mock idempotent gateway that records invocation IDs; assert single-effect-per-id across 5 retry waves.
TP-5: Canary run plan: 72h, 5% traffic divert, telemetry dashboard with automatic rollback if malformed-final-object delta > 0.02%.
TP-6: Security test: PII masking rules executed on strict and permissive payloads; verify no unmasked PII stored in logs during tests.
rollback_criteria: RC-1: If malformed-final-object rate increases by >0.02% relative to baseline during canary.
RC-2: If tool-call dedupe fails and duplicate side-effects observed in backend more than once per 50k requests.
RC-3: If resume-token misuse causes data-exposure or incorrect reassembly on >0.01% of requests.
RC-4: Security signoff not obtained for Private deployments.
notes_updates: 2026-02-12: Project kickoff — cross-functional sync between PM/Eng/Design. Agreed to add checkpoint token format and canonicalizer module in runtime.

2026-02-18: Eng spike completed — prototype canonicalization showed 4x CPU overhead for naive sort; engineering recommends streaming canonicalizer with incremental hashing to limit overhead (ENG-5987).
2026-02-25: Design feedback from Omar Patel — suggested final-object metadata UI surface to expose provenance and validation warnings. Added to Console ticket ENG-6342.

2026-03-01: Security review kickoff — initial threat model notes added (link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Sec/Structured+Output+Threat+Model). Security requested data-masking templates for PII.

2026-03-04: PM decision — default to permissive schema mode with strict opt-in. Rationale: reduce client breakage during rollout; enterprise customers can opt into strict for compliance. Follow-up: document migration path and examples.
2026-03-05: Code review feedback (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2097) — request to add integration test for duplicate-invocation edge-case; assigned to ENG QA.
Pending: finalize resume token format (binary vs base64), define canonical hash algorithm (sha256 canonical-json), sizing limits for fragments in Dedicated pools.
